html:
The Aseniwuche Winewak, Cree for Rocky Mountain people, are an Indigenous community around Grande Cache in the foothills of the Rockies in west central Alberta. Their ancestors were Cree, Iroquois, Secwepemc and Métis families who came together in the fur trade.

In the early 1800s the North West Company brought Iroquois men, many of them Mohawk, from the St. Lawrence to trap and guide in the Rockies. They married local Cree and other women and settled in the Athabasca valley around Jasper. After Jasper National Park was created in 1907, the families were made to leave, and they moved north to the Smoky River and Grande Cache.

They did not sign a treaty and are not a recognised band under the Indian Act, but they organised as the Aseniwuche Winewak Nation in the 1990s. Neighbours: Sturgeon Lake Cree. See also Métis.
